newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sends spending control bill to Congress.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sends spending control bill to Congress.

text.p: The Brazilian government Tuesday sent to Congress a bill seeking to control budget spending in 1998, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said.

Kandir told reporters the bill, which would establish general conditions for the yet-to-be drawn up 1998 federal government budget, would prohibit payroll increases and new construction, among other things, if approved by Congress.
It consists of eight main points, he said.
-- The bill would prohibit new hirings unless to fill vacant positions and only allows federal government agencies to contract staff if payroll costs do not exceed 60 percent of federal revenue.
-- It would prohibit the construction, extension or renovation of government buildings in 1998.
-- It would oblige all federal agencies to publish detailed lists of staff and their salaries.

-- It would limit total expenditure of the legislature and judiciary to average spending in the 1995 and 1996 financial years, not including one-off items such as building costs or special modernization programs.
-- The bill would establish tighter controls on the destination of funds raised to pay court-ordered settlements.
-- It would require ministries and government agencies to detail and control spending on medical and dental treatment for staff.
-- It establishes strict procedures for the National Treasury to pay rural credit.
-- The bill also creates conditions for some expenditure to be dependent on changes to tax law.
Kandir said six of the eight measures were aimed at controlling spending and said they were likely to ensure costs were cut. He did not give any estimates of potential savings.
